title: Green synthesis for novel azo-α,β-dehydroamino acid derivatives  via  ring-opening of azo-oxazolones: characterization, multimodal biological evaluation, and molecular docking studies
content: Nonproteinogenic α,β-dehydroamino acids (DHAAs) are key building blocks in peptidomimetic chemistry, as their backbone C═  C double bonds provide a crucial source of conformational constraint. In this context, a series of novel azo-α,β-dehydroamino acid derivatives 4(a–j) were synthesized via a rapid, environmentally friendly ring-opening reaction of azo-oxazolones with substituted aromatic amines in the presence of a weak acid–salt catalytic system. Derivative 4g demonstrated the highest sustainability, achieving a 98% isolated yield, which was corroborated by favorable green metrics (atom economy = 91.88% and E-factor = 6.5). All members of the series exhibited high chromatographic purity (>95%), as confirmed by high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Structural assignments were definitively established using FT-IR, 1H, 13C, and 19F NMR, EI-MS, UV-vis, and fluorescence spectroscopies. In vitro biological evaluations revealed significant antimicrobial, antioxidant, and anticancer activities. Specifically, compound 4b exhibited potent antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli, while compound 4h displayed the highest efficacy against Staphylococcus aureus, alongside substantial antifungal activity against Candida albicans and Cryptococcus neoformans. In DPPH radical scavenging assays, derivatives 4g, 4f, and 4h emerged as powerful antioxidants with IC50 values of 282.84, 287.84, and 297.95 µg mL−1, respectively (R2 > 0.99). Furthermore, derivatives 4h (IC50 = 65.66 µg mL−1) and 4f (IC50 = 124 µg mL−1) demonstrated significant cytotoxicity against MCF-7 breast cancer and HeLa cervical cancer cell lines, respectively. Molecular docking studies against DNA gyrase subunit B (PDB ID: 1KZN) revealed favorable binding affinities ranging from −8.1 to −8.8 kcal mol−1, with compound 4a exhibiting the highest score (−8.8 kcal mol−1). Additionally, in silico docking indicated promising binding interactions for 4h with ERα (−7.47 kcal mol−1) and 4f with HER2 (−8.9 kcal mol−1), computationally supporting their observed biological activities and highlighting their potential for future therapeutic development.
